title: Knowledge check: Development and Production Modes

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Development and Production Modes”?
options: Every component must call createApp separately.
The dist/ folder is the editable source of the app.
Vite reads production secrets from client code.
The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
questions.answer_key: The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Development and Production Modes directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Running the development server”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Edit generated dist assets as the source of truth.
Expose private credentials in client-side environment variables.
Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
Use Vue CLI as the primary new-project scaffolder without checking its status.
questions.answer_key: Use create-vue with Vite for new Vue projects, understand the SFC/entry-point roles, and test production builds separately from the dev server.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Running the development server”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Development and Production Modes” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
